parts.visual:
A user goes to Google and types: 'How to do payroll for 10 employees'. A startup that sells payroll software has written a massive, free, incredibly helpful guide on that exact topic. The user reads it, trusts the company, and buys the software.

The Strategy:
1. Content Marketing: Creating and distributing valuable, relevant content to attract and acquire a clearly defined audience.
2. SEO (Search Engine Optimization): The technical and strategic process of convincing Google's algorithm that your article is the absolute best answer on the internet, so you rank #1 for free.
parts.audio: Content marketing is the ultimate Inbound strategy. If you answer the internet's questions better than anyone else, Google will reward you with an infinite stream of free, highly-qualified customers.

questions.question: A startup writes 50 short, low-quality blog posts packed with the keyword 'best CRM software' hoping to trick Google. What will happen?
options: They will be penalized. Google's algorithm is extremely advanced. 'Keyword stuffing' is an ancient trick. If the content is low-quality and users instantly click away (High Bounce Rate), Google will bury the site on page 50.
questions.correct_answer: They will be penalized. Google's algorithm is extremely advanced. 'Keyword stuffing' is an ancient trick. If the content is low-quality and users instantly click away (High Bounce Rate), Google will bury the site on page 50.
questions.explanation: You must write for humans first, and algorithms second.

questions.question: Listen to the SEO expert explaining 'Backlinks'. Why are they so important?
questions.tts_text: You can write the best article in the world, but if the New York Times and Wikipedia don't link to it, Google doesn't trust it. A link from a highly respected website is like a massive 'vote of confidence' in the eyes of the algorithm.
options: Domain Authority. Google uses 'Backlinks' (other sites linking to yours) to measure trust. If highly authoritative sites link to your startup, Google assumes your startup is also an authority and boosts your rank.
questions.correct_answer: Domain Authority. Google uses 'Backlinks' (other sites linking to yours) to measure trust. If highly authoritative sites link to your startup, Google assumes your startup is also an authority and boosts your rank.
questions.explanation: Getting high-quality backlinks is the hardest and most valuable part of SEO.

questions.question: What is the danger of relying 100% on SEO for your startup's growth?
options: Platform Risk. You are building your entire business on land owned by Google. If Google changes its algorithm overnight, you could lose 90% of your traffic and go bankrupt in a week.
questions.correct_answer: Platform Risk. You are building your entire business on land owned by Google. If Google changes its algorithm overnight, you could lose 90% of your traffic and go bankrupt in a week.
questions.explanation: Never let one algorithm control the destiny of your company.

questions.question: What is a 'Long-Tail Keyword' strategy?
options: Instead of fighting giants to rank for 'Shoes', you try to rank for 'Best running shoes for flat feet marathon training'. The volume is lower, but the competition is zero and the 'intent to buy' is extremely high.
questions.correct_answer: Instead of fighting giants to rank for 'Shoes', you try to rank for 'Best running shoes for flat feet marathon training'. The volume is lower, but the competition is zero and the 'intent to buy' is extremely high.
questions.explanation: Startups win in the niches, not in the mainstream.
